You are auditing part of the admin portal of a real VPS hosting platform at /opt/nxeon. READ EVERY LINE of these files (use absolute paths, read the whole file, do not sample):

PAGES: /opt/nxeon/app/admin/servers/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/nodes/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/nodes/[id]/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/nodes/new/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/ips/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/provisioning/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/jobs/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/monitoring/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/infrastructure/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/abuse/page.tsx
COMPONENTS: /opt/nxeon/components/admin/NodeForms.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/NodeMetrics.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/IpPoolControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/AbuseActions.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/ServerConsole.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/BulkTable.tsx

For EVERY interactive control (button/form/select) find the server action it calls (in /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-*.ts) and verify the authorization check lives INSIDE the action function, not just in the UI. Known guard functions: requireArea(area), requireAdmin, requireStaff, assertNotImpersonating, ownedServer (allows ADMIN or owner). The relevant areas: servers/nodes/ips/provisioning/jobs/monitoring/abuse/infrastructure are all "fleet" area (ADMIN-only per lib/rbac.ts AREA_ROLES).

Report these defect classes with exact file:line:
1. A control whose backing server action has NO role/ownership guard, or a guard weaker than the page's area (a lower-privileged role could call it directly).
2. Destructive controls (delete node, delete server, release IP, suspend) missing a confirmation, or whose confirmation misstates the real consequence.
3. Displayed NUMBERS or STATUS indicators that are hardcoded, faked, or not actually computed from what they claim to measure (e.g. a hardcoded "operational", a capacity/count that doesn't match its query).
4. Missing audit() logging on consequential actions.

Do NOT edit anything. Do NOT run standalone node/prisma scripts. Return a concise list: each page with a one-line verdict (CLEAN or DEFECT), then each defect as file:line + what a malicious or lower-privileged operator could do. Quote the exact offending line.
